name: Scrawl
label: Simple Machines
lede: A Columbus trio that recorded at Prince's Paisley Park, bought back its own masters at auction, and still plays after forty years.

eras.title: Skull becomes Scrawl
eras.text: Marcy Mays and Sue Harshe, both from the ashes of a band called Skull, add a drummer and take a Columbus opening slot for the Meat Puppets. A $500 basement album follows.

years.h: Scrawl plays its first show, opening for the [[Meat Puppets|3df040ee-2b8b-446b-937a-3f86f4b2cabf]]
years.p: Drummer Carolyn O'Leary replaces Carla Sanseri just before the Columbus date. The band drops the name Skull, which Mays felt sounded too heavy metal.
years.xp: Mays and Harshe had met in Athens, Ohio in 1984. Wikipedia and Matter News both place the Meat Puppets opening slot (Stache's, per Matter News) at the start of the band's life.

years.p: Scrawl's debut LP comes out on No Other Records, cut in a friend's basement with volume limits. Robert Christgau's Village Voice review brings offers from Homestead, Twin/Tone and Rough Trade.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports the record cost under $500. Matter News says it was made in a friend's basement where they had to keep the volume down.

eras.title: The Rough Trade detour
eras.text: Scrawl takes the Rough Trade offer and records at Prince's Paisley Park, then watches the label go under.

years.h: Recording He's Drunk at Prince's Paisley Park
years.p: Signed to Rough Trade after a CBGB show Mays remembers as one of their worst, Scrawl cut He's Drunk in Minneapolis.
years.xp: Harshe told Matter News they saw Prince's labeled meat refrigerator but never met him. Wikipedia says the record had sold about 4,000 copies by 1990.

years.h: Smallmouth, cut after O'Leary breaks her arm
years.p: Producer Gary Smith recorded it in November 1989; Harshe calls the sessions bizarre.

years.h: Rough Trade goes bankrupt; Scrawl buys back its own masters
years.p: With the label in bankruptcy, the band bought its master tapes at a public auction.

eras.title: Albini, and a new drummer
eras.text: Scrawl pays for its own record, records with Steve Albini, and loses O'Leary.

years.p: Released on Feel Good All Over, the EP's 2,000-copy first pressing sold out fast. Village Voice's Pazz & Jop poll ranked it ninth among EPs.
years.xp: At Length quotes the liner note: the band paid for the session because it was tired of waiting on faxes, calls and contracts from the bankrupt label.

years.h: Scrawl plays the Kill Rock Stars festival in Olympia
years.p: Alongside [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] and [[Bikini Kill|1397d045-1603-41fc-80b9-712c18360145]], per At Length; the band later got tagged as riot grrrl and foxcore precursors, labels they distrusted.
years.xp: Kathleen Hanna cited Scrawl as an influence, per Wikipedia. Tsunami's Jenny Toomey has called them an enormous influence on how her band worked.

years.h: Carolyn O'Leary leaves; Scrawl tours as an acoustic duo
years.p: Mays and Harshe played acoustic until they found [[Dana Marshall|3f1a27a7-6575-426c-9d25-c83afd27ff93]] on drums by the end of the year.

years.h: Scrawl signs to Simple Machines and Southern (UK)
years.p: Dana Marshall's arrival and the new deal come together by year's end.

eras.title: Simple Machines years
eras.text: The Simple Machines run: a split single with Versus and the record most fans call the band's best, Velvet Hammer.

years.p: Scrawl's "January" shares a Simple Machines single with Versus.

years.src: Wikipedia · Matter News · New York Times
years.h: Velvet Hammer, with Albini back at the board
years.p: Recorded in January 1993 and released November 8 by Simple Machines, it opens with "Your Mother Wants to Know".
years.xp: Harshe praised Albini to Matter News as the first engineer who was not hired by a record label. The New York Times said Mays's guitar and Harshe's bass sometimes stand apart, sometimes mesh for buzzing riffs, and Entertainment Weekly gave it an A-.

years.h: European tour, including the Reading Festival
years.p: Scrawl plays the UK festival on a European run behind Velvet Hammer.

eras.title: The Elektra years
eras.text: Elektra signs Scrawl, then drops the band by fax. Marshall plays his last show in 2000.

years.h: Travel On, Rider, their major label debut
years.p: Terry Tolkin signs Scrawl to Elektra. Wikipedia reports it sold 2,115 copies.

years.big: Postcards to the boss: Disgusted, Relieved, or Out of the Closet
years.h: Elektra drops Scrawl by fax, six weeks after Nature Film
years.p: Scrawl re-recorded six Rough Trade-era songs and a Public Image Ltd cover for Nature Film. After the fax, they mailed fans postcards for label head Sylvia Rhone.
years.xp:
Over 250 supporters sent Sylvia Rhone a postcard reproducing the fax, with checkboxes labeled Disgusted, Relieved, Out of the Closet and Other. Wikipedia reports Nature Film sold 956 copies.

Harshe said re-recording old songs made sense because giving Elektra 12 new ones seemed depressing.

years.h: Dana Marshall plays his last show, then moves to Sweden
years.p: The trio goes quiet; Mays and Harshe play acoustic in 2001.

eras.title: Still here
eras.text: Scrawl regroups for a club anniversary and keeps coming back.

years.h: Reunion for Little Brother's 10th anniversary in Columbus
years.p: Jovan Karcic of Gaunt takes over on drums. Harshe also starts Fort Shame that year.

years.h: Monthly sessions on instrumentals and a free show in Franklinton
years.p: Matter News reported the trio was building instrumental material for a possible album, and played Secret Studio on September 30.

years.h: DromFest again, with Tsunami's Luther Gray on drums
years.p: Karcic could not make it, so [[Tsunami|fea43e99-c4d5-4dac-9c27-868e864c6dc2]]'s Luther Gray filled in. They also played DromFest in 2024.
